newsitem.title: USA: Agents roust guests at Clinton hotel.
newsitem.headline: Agents roust guests at Clinton hotel.

text.p: Secret Service agents at a New Hampshire hotel where President Bill Clinton stayed Sunday night rousted hotel guests from their beds in the middle of the night for security checks.

An official, who asked not to be identified, said members of the president's travelling party, a group that includes campaign staff, members of the media and White House support personnel, were awakened by agents at the Tara Wayfarer Inn, previously named the Sheraton Wayfarer.

He said a furious White House Deputy Chief of Staff Harold Ickes, who was not among those disturbed, was demanding an explanation from the U.S. Secret Service, which is charged with protecting the president.
The official said he was rousted from bed and made to stand in the hotel hallway while Secret Service agents and Army ordinance experts with bomb-sniffing dogs checked his room for explosives.
Clinton arrived at the hotel shortly after 3. a.m. EST after a post-midnight campaign rally in Bangor, Maine.
Secret Service spokesman Carl Meyer called the incident "an unfortunate situation."

Because of the stretching of Secret Service resources in the campaign's final, hectic days, Meyer said agents had checked out those rooms they were certain would be occupied before midnight, leaving those they thought would be left vacant until Clinton arrived for later checks.
"According to the information provided to us, the rooms were supposed to be vacant but (the) people who occupied the rooms changed their plans and we were not informed," he said.

The 194-room Manchester inn has often hosted presidential candidates as well as large numbers of journalists, notably ahead of the New Hampshire presidential primary in February, one of the first key tests of a candidate's support.
While such incidents are rare on the campaign trail, they are not unheard of.
A similar incident occurred two weeks ago in Ohio at the Rennaissance Cleveland Hotel, where at least three journalists were awakened in the middle of the night for such searches.
